## Context
Bridge fsck reported unbound Jira issues. ACLI inspection on 2026-08-16 proved the remaining three are not Jira-native work to adopt or archive: each is an exact identity match for an existing local `code_review` artifact, including `rebar-id` label, title, revision, PASS decision, and fingerprint. The missing state was only the forward/reverse binding-store entries.

## Exact mappings
- `a750-2710-e903-4a45` (`firstborn-removable-javalina`) ↔ `REB-806`
- `d494-d34f-cf36-43df` (`festive-egotistic-terrier`) ↔ `REB-807`
- `ee21-fcd3-edad-462c` (`impossible-censorian-kangaroo`) ↔ `REB-808`

## Executed remediation
- Claimed this ticket before changing shared tracker state.
- Under `rebar._store.lock.write_lock`, verified fsck still reported exactly the three alerting unbound Jira keys with no other alerting or integrity findings.
- Re-read local artifacts and live Jira issues through ACLI; exact identities still matched.
- Called public `BindingStore.bind_confirm` for each exact pair, atomically saved, and published with `commit_and_push_tickets_branch(strict=True)`.
- Re-read every forward/reverse mapping and re-ran fsck.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `REB-806`, `REB-807`, and `REB-808` map bidirectionally to the three exact existing local code-review tickets listed above.
- [x] No new local ticket or Jira issue is created, archived, or transitioned.
- [x] The mutation runs under rebar’s unified tracker write lock and publishes through the supported commit-and-push seam.
- [x] `rebar bridge fsck` reports no alerting `binding_drift` and no `store_integrity` findings after repair.
- [x] A ticket comment records the guarded before/after evidence and delivered tracker commit.
